unit.why: A teaching by the Apter Rav on the danger young men face when travelling to a tzaddik, followed by the author's first-person memorate of his awe before his uncle and master, who embraced him and swore to him by his beard on a Sabbath eve.
unit.boundary_note: the narrative part is a short memorate wrapped in a homiletic frame; a borderline case between story and teaching

stories.summary_en: The Apter Rav warns that young men who come to a tzaddik without awe are 'extinguished' and become opponents. The author recalls that his uncle and master always showed him love, yet he trembled before him and stood at the door unable to enter. Through this awe he stayed bound to the master, who swore by his holy beard on a Sabbath eve never to abandon him.
